title: Scripts missing executable permission
description: scripts/ci-install-godot.sh and scripts/test-godot-compat.sh lack the executable bit (mode 644 instead of 755). The test-godot-compat.sh usage docs say to run './scripts/test-godot-compat.sh' which will fail with 'Permission denied' without chmod +x. The CI workflow works around this by calling 'bash scripts/...' explicitly, but the test-addon-install.sh (which does have +x) is inconsistent with the other two. Introduced in commits acfaac6 and fb78bc6. Build SHA: fb78bc6.

title: save_baseline/screenshot_diff selector never crops
description:
In tools_visual.go, the captureScreenshot helper (used by handleSaveBaseline and handleScreenshotDiff) hardcodes full_page: true (line 108). The GDScript screenshot_capture.gd only crops when 'not full_page and params.has("selector")' (line 21). This means the 'selector' parameter in godot_screenshot_save_baseline and godot_screenshot_diff is documented as 'Crop to this node's bounding rect' (skills/stagehand.md lines 257, 271) but has no effect -- screenshots always capture the full viewport regardless of selector.

Repro: Call godot_screenshot_save_baseline(name="test", selector="class:Panel") -- the saved image will be full viewport, not cropped to Panel.

Fix: captureScreenshot should pass full_page: false (or omit it) when a selector is present.

Build SHA: 3299725

title: godot_connect leaks connection on ping failure
description:
In internal/mcpserver/tools_lifecycle.go, handleConnect stores the connection at line 36 via setConn(conn), then sends a ping at line 39. If the ping fails (e.g., Godot responds with an error, or the WebSocket drops during ping), the function returns the error but leaves the broken connection stored in s.conn. 

Repro: Connect to a WebSocket endpoint that accepts the TCP handshake but closes before responding to the ping RPC.

Expected: On ping failure, the connection should be cleared so the server reports "not connected" and the user can retry.
Actual: The stale connection remains stored. Subsequent tool calls get confusing errors from the broken connection rather than the clear "Not connected. Call godot_connect or godot_launch first." message.

Build SHA: d5acb55
File: internal/mcpserver/tools_lifecycle.go:36-42

title: Record-replay tools missing GDScript handlers
description: The Go MCP tools godot_record_start, godot_record_stop, and godot_replay (internal/mcpserver/tools_record.go) send JSON-RPC methods record_start, record_stop, and replay to the Godot addon via callGodot(). However, the GDScript addon (addons/stagehand/autoload/stagehand_server.gd) has no handlers registered for these methods in _register_builtin_handlers() (lines 138-157), and there is no implementation code for recording/replaying in any .gd file. All three tools will fail at runtime with Method not found. The Go E2E tests pass because they use a stub (e2e_test.go lines 196-200) that returns canned responses, masking the missing server-side implementation. Introduced in commit 814653f. Build SHA: fb78bc6.

title: Addon errors not surfaced as MCP errors
description:
## Summary
Most MCP tool handlers do not call `checkGodotResult()` on the raw JSON
returned by the Godot addon. When the addon returns a handler-level error
like `{"error": "Node not found"}`, the MCP response is marked as
success (`IsError=false`) and the error JSON is passed through as plain
text. MCP clients cannot distinguish addon errors from successful results.

## Affected handlers
All handlers in tools_query.go, tools_input.go, tools_method.go,
tools_wait.go, tools_property.go, tools_performance.go, tools_record.go,
and tools_lifecycle.go (handleGetGameState). Only tools_visual.go
(screenshot handlers) correctly calls `checkGodotResult()`.

## Repro steps
1. Connect to a running Godot game via `godot_connect`
2. Call `godot_find_nodes` with `selector: "class:NonExistent"`
3. Godot returns `{"nodes":[],"count":0}` -- this is fine (not an error)
4. Call `godot_get_property` with a selector that matches but a
   property that doesn't exist
5. Godot returns `{"error": "Property not found: bogus"}`
6. Expected: MCP result has `IsError=true` with the error message
7. Actual: MCP result has `IsError=false` with the raw JSON text

## Impact
MCP clients (like Claude) see error responses as successful tool calls,
making automated test flows unreliable -- errors are silently swallowed.

title: test-godot-compat.sh uses stale ERROR grep
description: scripts/test-godot-compat.sh line 61 uses the broad grep pattern 'ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|Parse Error' that was specifically narrowed in the CI pipeline (commit e05e201, merged f80248f) to just 'SCRIPT ERROR|Parse Error'. The CI comment explains: headless Godot emits harmless engine-level ERROR lines (Vulkan, display driver) on runners. The compat test script was added later in fb78bc6 but copied the old broad pattern. This causes false failures when running locally or in CI environments with GPU/display ERROR messages. title: Flush active recording on server stop
description: When the Stagehand server stops (via _stop() called from _exit_tree), it does not flush an active recording. If the user started a recording via record_start and the game exits before record_stop, the recorded frames are silently discarded. The _stop() method in stagehand_server.gd should check if _recorder.is_recording() and call stop_recording() to flush to disk. The input_recorder.gd _exit_tree handler should also flush rather than just clearing state. NOTE: This replaces godot-stagehand-5vh which conflicted with the 232 record-replay handlers merge. Start from current main (SHA 5fa1a85) which already has _ensure_recorder() and StagehandInputRecorder. Build on the existing architecture — do not rewrite the replay logic.

title: Active recording lost on server stop
description: When the Stagehand server stops (via _stop() called from _exit_tree), it does not call _recorder.stop_recording(). If the user started a recording via record_start and the game exits or the server is stopped before record_stop is called, the recorded frames are silently discarded. The input_recorder.gd _exit_tree handler (line 22-24) sets _recording=false and _frames=[] but does NOT flush to disk. This is data loss for the user. The _stop() method in stagehand_server.gd (line 442) should check if _recorder is active and flush the recording. Introduced in commit e641ba4. Build SHA: 877e8ed. Files: addons/stagehand/autoload/stagehand_server.gd:442-451, addons/stagehand/core/input_recorder.gd:22-24.

title: Unchecked type assertions panic on bad input
description:
Three unchecked type assertions in internal/mcpserver/tools_input.go (lines 42, 169, 265) will panic and crash the MCP server if a client sends a non-string value for the 'selector' parameter.

Repro: Send a godot_click, godot_type_text, or godot_mouse_move request with selector set to a non-string value (e.g. {"selector": 123}).

Expected: Returns an MCP error result indicating invalid parameter type.
Actual: Server panics with "interface conversion: interface {} is float64, not string".

All three use the unsafe form `selector.(string)` instead of the safe comma-ok form `sel, ok := selector.(string)`. Compare with the test code in e2e_test.go which correctly uses the safe form.

Introduced in c3477a1 (2026-05-14). Build SHA: d5acb55.

Affected lines:
- tools_input.go:42 (handleClick)
- tools_input.go:169 (handleTypeText)
- tools_input.go:265 (handleMouseMove)

title: Connection lifecycle is confusing and finicky in multi-session use
description:
## Summary

The architecture of stdio MCP process → shared WebSocket → single Godot game is unclear to users and causes practical friction:

- Multiple MCP processes can connect to the same Godot game with no coordination
- Stale processes linger in the background when sessions end, and new sessions unknowingly share the game
- No visibility into who/what is currently connected
- No clear "clean slate" workflow — users end up with ghost connections they don't know about

## User Feedback

"Feels hard to set up and finicky in practice."

## Possible Improvements

- Document the architecture clearly (one Go process per MCP client, all share one game via WS)
- Add a `godot_status` tool showing connection state and other connected clients
- Auto-disconnect or timeout idle connections
- Consider a session/lock model so only one MCP client "owns" the game at a time
- Detect and warn if another process is already connected to the same game
- Graceful cleanup when the stdio pipe closes (parent session ends)

title: Legacy Parse() silently misclassifies new selectors
description:
## Summary
The `selector.Parse()` function (legacy API) does not recognize text:,
meta:, or unique: prefixes. When given e.g. "text:Submit", it falls
through to the default case and returns a Path selector with value
"text:Submit" instead of erroring or returning a Text selector.

While `Parse()` is not called in production (all production code uses
`ParseChain()`), it remains exported and available for external callers.
Its silent misclassification is a trap: any external consumer or future
internal caller using `Parse("text:Submit")` would get a Path selector
that queries for a node at path "text:Submit" -- which will never match.

## Repro
    s, err := selector.Parse("text:Submit")
    // err is nil -- no error
    // s.Type == Path, s.Value == "text:Submit"
    // Expected: s.Type == Text, s.Value == "Submit"

## Recommendation
Either make Parse() support all selector types (like
parseSingleSelectorAllTypes does), or deprecate/unexport it so
external callers don't hit this silently.

## Files
- `/home/mrf/Projects/godot-stagehand/internal/selector/parse.go` lines 86-112

title: godot_wait_for_signal skips selector validation
description: In internal/mcpserver/tools_wait.go, handleWaitForSignal (lines 76-98) does not call validateSelector() on the selector parameter before sending it to Godot. Both handleWaitForNode (line 40) and handleWaitForProperty (line 138) call validateSelector(), but handleWaitForSignal omits it. This means malformed selectors bypass Go-side validation and are sent directly to the Godot addon, which may produce confusing errors or unexpected behavior. Introduced in commit 077c1e1. title: Make GDScript addon strict-mode compliant
description:
The Stagehand GDScript addon fails to load in host projects that have strict GDScript warnings-as-errors enabled (e.g. water-wars). All 6+ .gd files need fixes.

## Errors observed (stagehand_server.gd alone has 23 errors):
- Implicitly inferred static types on consts/vars (`:=` without type annotation)
- `float()`, `int()`, `bool()` constructors called with Variant args
- Return values discarded (erase(), send_text(), stop_recording())
- String() constructor with Variant arg (should use str())
- Variable shadowing Node.name
- Performance.Monitor enum vs Variant type mismatch
- Viewport.size not present on base Viewport type
- Ternary with incompatible types (String vs null)
- Coroutine called without await
- Dictionary values accessed as Variant when .close() needed

## Files affected:
- autoload/stagehand_server.gd (23+ errors)
- core/waiter.gd (15+ inferred types, untyped params)
- core/selector_engine.gd (many := inferred types, untyped lambda vars)
- core/input_simulator.gd (float() constructor issues, := inferred types)
- core/input_recorder.gd (float/int/bool constructor issues, := inferred types)
- protocol/json_rpc.gd (few := inferred types)

## Acceptance criteria:
1. All .gd files pass `godot --check-only` with strict warnings-as-errors
2. Add strict-mode validation to CI/test pipeline (run against a project with all warnings elevated to errors)
3. copy-addon.sh test includes strict-mode check

title: CI grep ERROR pattern causes false positives
description: The GDScript parse check in .github/workflows/ci.yml (line 70) and scripts/test-godot-compat.sh (line 61) use grep -qE 'ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|Parse Error' to detect failures. The bare 'ERROR' pattern matches any Godot log line containing the word ERROR anywhere, including harmless engine messages during headless startup (e.g. Vulkan/display driver warnings, 'ERROR: Condition ... is true' from the engine internals). This will cause false positive CI failures on runners where headless Godot emits these common startup warnings. The pattern should be narrowed to match only GDScript-specific errors, e.g. 'SCRIPT ERROR' and 'Parse Error', or filter out known benign patterns. Introduced in commits acfaac6 and fb78bc6. Build SHA: fb78bc6.

title: Screenshot crop incomplete in handleScreenshot
description:
The fix in commit 511407f ("Fix screenshot crop: set full_page=false when selector present") only applied the fix to the internal captureScreenshot helper (used by save_baseline and screenshot_diff) but NOT to handleScreenshot (the direct godot_screenshot tool handler).

In tools_visual.go:70-79, handleScreenshot reads full_page from the request (default true) and passes it through. When a user calls godot_screenshot with a selector but omits full_page, the addon receives full_page=true with a selector present. The GDScript addon (screenshot_capture.gd line 21) only crops when full_page is false AND selector is present. Result: the selector is silently ignored and a full viewport screenshot is returned.

Expected: godot_screenshot with a selector should automatically set full_page=false (as captureScreenshot does at line 114).
Actual: full_page remains true, selector is ignored by the addon.

Repro: call godot_screenshot with {"selector": "class:Button"} (no explicit full_page).

title: godot_mouse_move always fails: handler not registered
description: The Go MCP server's handleMouseMove (tools_input.go:279) sends method "input_mouse_move" via callGodot, but the Godot addon (stagehand_server.gd _register_builtin_handlers) never registers an "input_mouse_move" handler. The function StagehandInputSimulator.input_mouse_move() exists in input_simulator.gd:312 but is never wired up to the command router. Any call to godot_mouse_move will return 'Method not found: input_mouse_move'. Build SHA: 68d04b2.

title: handleConnect closes conn outside mutex
description: In tools_lifecycle.go line 28-30, handleConnect calls s.getConn() (which acquires/releases RLock), then calls existing.Close() without holding any lock, then later calls s.setConn(). Between getConn() returning and Close() completing, another goroutine could also call getConn() and get the same Connection pointer, then attempt to use it (e.g. via callGodot). This is a race condition window. Compare with clearConn() in server.go which correctly holds the write lock while closing. Also compare with handleLaunch which uses the pattern killExistingLaunch() (properly locked) + separate getConn/Close. The handleConnect pattern should use clearConn() instead of the manual get-then-close. Build SHA: 877e8ed. File: internal/mcpserver/tools_lifecycle.go:28-30.

title: Phase 3: Production-ready automation platform
description:
## Goal

Take Godot Stagehand from beta to production-ready. Phase 2 delivered the core tool set. Phase 3 adds the features that make it reliable for real CI pipelines, accessible games, and professional test workflows.

## Themes

1. **Reliability** — Signal waiting, error normalization, GDScript test coverage
2. **Observability** — Performance profiling, visual regression
3. **Accessibility** — AccessKit integration for Godot 4.5+
4. **Workflow** — Record-and-replay, CI/CD integration
5. **Scale** — Multi-instance testing for networked games

## Definition of Done

- All Phase 3 tools from DESIGN.md implemented with full test coverage
- GDScript addon has GdUnit4 unit tests for every handler
- CI pipeline runs tests automatically on PR
- Visual regression baseline established
- Documentation covers all tools with real-world examples
- Addon installation verified on Godot 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5

## Quality Standards

ALL work on Phase 3 children MUST follow strict TDD:
1. Write a failing test FIRST (Go unit/E2E or GdUnit4)
2. Implement the minimum code to pass
3. Refactor if needed
4. Run full suite — no regressions allowed
5. Run code-simplifier agent before committing

No PR merges without passing tests. No skipped tests. No "TODO: add test later."

title: godot_wait_for_signal — signal-based waiting with timeout
description:
## Feature

Implement `godot_wait_for_signal` MCP tool — wait for a specific Godot signal to be emitted on a node, with timeout.

## Design (from DESIGN.md)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| selector | string | yes | | Node that emits the signal |
| signal_name | string | yes | | Signal to wait for |
| timeout_ms | int | no | 5000 | |

Returns: `{ received, elapsed_ms, args }`

## Implementation

### GDScript (waiter.gd)
- Use one-shot signal connection: `node.signal_name.connect(callback, CONNECT_ONE_SHOT)`
- Start a Timer for timeout
- Return signal args if received, or `{received: false, reason: "timeout"}` if timer fires first
- Clean up: disconnect signal if timeout fires, stop timer if signal fires

### GWP Method
- Method name: `wait_signal`
- Params: `{selector, signal_name, timeout_ms}`
- Response: `{received, elapsed_ms, args}`

### Go MCP Tool
- Tool name: `godot_wait_for_signal`
- Pass through to GWP `wait_signal` method
- Validate selector with ParseChain() before sending

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GDScript handler with one-shot signal + timer timeout
- [ ] Go MCP tool registered with correct parameter schema
- [ ] E2E test with stub (signal received + timeout cases)
- [ ] Integration test: emit a signal from test scene, verify it's captured
- [ ] Edge case: signal emitted before wait starts (should timeout, not crash)
- [ ] Edge case: node freed while waiting (should return error, not crash)

## TDD Protocol

1. Write Go E2E test expecting `wait_signal` GWP method — fails (not in stub)
2. Add stub case, test passes
3. Write GdUnit4 test for waiter signal handler — fails
4. Implement GDScript handler, test passes
5. Integration test with real Godot

title: Godot version compatibility matrix — test addon on 4.2-4.5
description:
## Goal

Verify addon compatibility across Godot versions. The addon-breaks-compilation bug (vv2.17) showed that GDScript APIs vary between Godot 4.x versions. We need a compatibility matrix.

## Versions to Test

- Godot 4.2 (oldest supported)
- Godot 4.3
- Godot 4.4 (current stable)
- Godot 4.5 (beta, AccessKit)

## Test Protocol

For each version:
1. Install addon into clean Godot project
2. Open project in editor — no parse errors
3. Run project headless with STAGEHAND_ENABLED=1 — server starts
4. Connect from Go binary — ping succeeds
5. Exercise core tools (get_tree, find_nodes, click, screenshot)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test script that downloads each Godot version and runs the protocol
- [ ] Known incompatibilities documented in README
- [ ] Minimum supported version declared in plugin.cfg or README
- [ ] CI matrix tests at least 2 Godot versions

title: Addon installation smoke test — verify addon doesn't break host projects
description:
## Goal

Automated smoke test that installs the addon into a real Godot project and verifies the project still compiles. This is the test that would have caught vv2.17 before manual testing.

## Implementation

2. Launch Godot headless with \`--check-only\` (or \`--headless --quit\` + check exit code)

- Copies addon, runs Godot, checks exit code

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test runs in CI pipeline (depends on CI task)
- [ ] Any GDScript parse error fails the test with clear output

## Dependencies

title: godot_touch — touch event simulation for mobile games
description:
## Feature

Implement `godot_touch` MCP tool — simulate touch events for mobile/touch-based games.

## Design

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| position | {x, y} | yes | | Touch position |
| index | int | no | 0 | Touch finger index (for multi-touch) |
| action | string | no | "tap" | "tap", "press", "release", "drag" |
| drag_to | {x, y} | no | | End position for drag action |
| duration_ms | int | no | 100 | Hold duration for tap/press |

Returns: `{ success }`

### GWP Method: `input_touch`
### GDScript: Use `InputEventScreenTouch` and `InputEventScreenDrag`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Go MCP tool with parameter validation
- [ ] E2E test with stub
- [ ] Integration test for tap and drag
- [ ] Multi-touch index support

title: GDScript unit test suite — GdUnit4 tests for all addon modules
description:
## Problem

The GDScript addon has ZERO unit tests. DESIGN.md specifies GdUnit4 tests for all core modules but none exist. This is a quality gap that means GDScript bugs (like the error_string and parent.tree issues) go undetected until manual testing.

## Scope

Write GdUnit4 test suites for every module in `addons/stagehand/core/`:

### Test files to create:
1. `test/test_selector_engine.gd` — Each selector type (path, name, class, group, text, meta, unique), chaining with >>, edge cases (empty string, invalid prefix, no matches)
2. `test/test_tree_serializer.gd` — Serialize simple tree, deep tree, property inclusion, max_depth cutoff
3. `test/test_input_simulator.gd` — Correct InputEvent types created for mouse/key/action/text/touch
4. `test/test_property_handler.gd` — Get/set simple props, dot notation (position.x), missing node, missing prop
5. `test/test_method_handler.gd` — Allowed methods, blocklist enforcement, private method rejection
6. `test/test_expression_evaluator.gd` — Simple expressions, context node, error handling
7. `test/test_waiter.gd` — Node existence, property conditions, timeout behavior
8. `test/test_json_rpc.gd` — Parse request, construct response, construct error, malformed input
9. `test/test_command_router.gd` — Register handler, route method, unknown method error
10. `test/test_scene_handler.gd` — Valid scene path, invalid scene path

### Infrastructure:
- GdUnit4 addon installed in test_project
- Test runner script that can be invoked from Go integration tests
- Each test file uses `extends GdUnitTestSuite`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 10 test files exist and pass
- [ ] Tests cover happy path + at least 2 error cases per module
- [ ] Tests run in headless mode via GdUnit4 CLI
- [ ] Go integration test can invoke GdUnit4 runner and parse results
- [ ] Zero skip, zero pending — every test either passes or fails

## TDD Note

These ARE the tests — write them to fail against current code first. Fix any bugs the tests surface as separate commits with the bug ID in the message.

title: Accessibility tree integration (AccessKit on Godot 4.5+)
description:
## Feature

Integrate with Godot 4.5+'s AccessKit accessibility tree to provide semantic game state queries. Instead of relying only on node paths and class names, agents could query the accessibility tree for roles, labels, and relationships.

## Background

Godot 4.5 adds AccessKit support for Control nodes (screen reader support). This exposes an accessibility tree parallel to the scene tree, with semantic information like roles (button, text field, label), accessible names, and states (focused, pressed, expanded).

## Design

### New MCP Tool: `godot_get_accessibility_tree`
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| root_path | string | no | "/root" | Subtree root |
| max_depth | int | no | 10 | Recursion depth |

Returns: `{ nodes: [{role, name, value, state, path, children}] }`

### New selector prefix: `role:`
| Prefix | Example | Matches |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `role:` | `"role:button"` | Nodes with AccessKit role "button" |

### GDScript Implementation
- Check Godot version >= 4.5 at runtime
- Use AccessKit bridge APIs to enumerate accessible nodes
- Fall back gracefully on Godot < 4.5 with clear error message

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `godot_get_accessibility_tree` tool returns semantic tree
- [ ] `role:` selector works for Control nodes
- [ ] Graceful fallback on Godot < 4.5 (clear "not available" message)
- [ ] E2E tests with stub
- [ ] Integration test on Godot 4.5+ headless

## Dependencies

- Requires Godot 4.5+ (feature-detect at runtime)
- AccessKit API surface may still be unstable — pin to specific Godot version for testing

## TDD Protocol

1. Write Go E2E test for `godot_get_accessibility_tree` — fails
2. Implement stub + Go handler — passes
3. Write GdUnit4 test for accessibility bridge (skip on < 4.5) — fails
4. Implement GDScript — passes

title: Visual regression testing — screenshot diffing with baseline management
description:
## Feature

Screenshot-based visual regression testing. Compare current screenshots against baseline images and report pixel differences.

## Design

### New MCP Tool: `godot_screenshot_diff`
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| selector | string | no | | Crop to node rect |
| baseline_path | string | yes | | Path to baseline PNG |
| threshold | float | no | 0.01 | Max allowed difference (0.0-1.0) |
| output_diff_path | string | no | | Path to write diff image |

Returns: `{ match, difference_pct, diff_image_base64, pixel_count_different }`

### New MCP Tool: `godot_screenshot_save_baseline`
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| selector | string | no | | Crop to node rect |
| path | string | yes | | Path to save baseline PNG |

Returns: `{ saved, path, width, height }`

### Implementation

- Go-side image comparison using `image` stdlib (no external deps)
- Pixel-by-pixel RGBA diff with configurable threshold
- Generate diff image highlighting changed pixels in red
- Baseline management: save/update/compare workflow

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `godot_screenshot_save_baseline` captures and saves PNG
- [ ] `godot_screenshot_diff` compares current vs baseline
- [ ] Difference percentage calculated correctly
- [ ] Diff image generated showing changed regions
- [ ] Threshold parameter controls pass/fail sensitivity
- [ ] Unit tests for image comparison logic (Go, no Godot needed)
- [ ] E2E test with stub for both tools

## TDD Protocol

1. Write Go unit tests for image diff algorithm with test fixtures — fails
2. Implement image comparison in new `internal/imgdiff/` package — passes
3. Write E2E tests for MCP tools — fails
4. Implement tool handlers — passes

title: Record-and-replay mode — capture and replay input sessions
description:
## Feature

Record user interactions (input events) during a game session and replay them deterministically for automated testing. Like Playwright's codegen but for Godot games.

## Design

### New MCP Tools

**`godot_record_start`**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| output_path | string | no | | File path to save recording |
| include_mouse_move | bool | no | false | Record mouse movement (verbose) |

Returns: `{ recording, session_id }`

**`godot_record_stop`**
Returns: `{ session_id, events_count, duration_ms, path }`

**`godot_replay`**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| recording_path | string | yes | | Path to recording file |
| speed | float | no | 1.0 | Playback speed multiplier |
| wait_for_ready | bool | no | true | Wait for scene to be ready before replaying |

Returns: `{ replayed, events_count, duration_ms }`

### GDScript Implementation
- Hook into `_input()` to capture all InputEvents during recording
- Serialize events with timestamps to JSON
- Replay by injecting events through `Input.parse_input_event()` with timing
- Support speed multiplier for fast CI runs

### Recording Format (JSON)
```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "start_scene": "res://scenes/main.tscn",
  "engine_version": "4.3.0",
  "events": [
    {"t_ms": 0, "type": "key", "key": "W", "pressed": true},
    {"t_ms": 150, "type": "key", "key": "W", "pressed": false},
    {"t_ms": 500, "type": "mouse", "position": {"x": 512, "y": 300}, "button": "left"}
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Record captures all input types (key, mouse, action, touch)
- [ ] Replay reproduces input sequence with correct timing
- [ ] Speed multiplier works for fast CI runs
- [ ] Recording file format is documented and versioned
- [ ] E2E tests with stub for all 3 tools
- [ ] Integration test: record a click sequence, replay it, verify state changes

## TDD Protocol

Standard: E2E tests first (fail), stub + handler (pass), GdUnit4 tests (fail), GDScript (pass), integration test.

title: Performance profiling tools — FPS, frame time, memory monitoring
description:
## Feature

Performance profiling tools that let agents and CI pipelines monitor game performance metrics during automation runs.

## Design

### New MCP Tool: `godot_get_performance`
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| metrics | string[] | no | ["fps","frame_time","physics_time"] | Which metrics to return |

Returns: `{ fps, frame_time_ms, physics_time_ms, render_time_ms, memory_static_mb, memory_dynamic_mb, object_count, node_count, orphan_node_count }`

### New MCP Tool: `godot_assert_performance`
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| min_fps | float | no | | Minimum acceptable FPS |
| max_frame_time_ms | float | no | | Maximum frame time |
| max_memory_mb | float | no | | Maximum memory usage |
| duration_ms | int | no | 1000 | Sampling duration |

Returns: `{ passed, violations: [{metric, expected, actual, timestamp}], samples }`

### GDScript Implementation
- Use `Performance` singleton: `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_FPS)`, etc.
- Sample over duration for assert_performance
- Return all available Performance monitors

### GWP Methods: `get_performance`, `assert_performance`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `godot_get_performance` returns current metrics snapshot
- [ ] `godot_assert_performance` samples over duration and reports violations
- [ ] All standard Godot Performance monitors exposed
- [ ] E2E tests with stub
- [ ] Integration test reads real FPS from headless Godot

## TDD Protocol

Standard: E2E test → stub → GdUnit4 test → GDScript → integration test.

title: CI/CD pipeline — GitHub Actions for Go + GDScript + integration tests
description:
## Goal

GitHub Actions CI pipeline that runs on every PR and push to main. Ensures no regressions land.

## Pipeline Stages

### 1. Go Quality (fast, ~30s)
- \`go vet ./...\`
- \`go test ./...\` (unit + E2E with mock WebSocket)
- Build binary for linux/amd64

### 2. GDScript Quality (medium, ~60s)
- Install Godot headless (cache in Actions)
- Parse-check all .gd files: \`godot --headless --check-only\` (or equivalent)
- Run GdUnit4 test suite

### 3. Integration Tests (slow, ~120s)
- Build binary
- Launch Godot headless with test_project
- Run Go integration tests against real Godot
- Collect and upload test artifacts (screenshots, logs)

### 4. Build Matrix
- Go: linux/amd64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64
- Godot: 4.2, 4.3, 4.4 (4.5 when stable)

## Files to Create

- \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` — Main CI pipeline
- \`.github/workflows/release.yml\` — Tagged release builds
- \`scripts/ci-install-godot.sh\` — Download + cache Godot headless

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PR checks run Go tests + vet
- [ ] PR checks validate GDScript parses cleanly
- [ ] PR checks run GdUnit4 tests (when test suite exists)
- [ ] Integration tests run on main branch pushes
- [ ] Build matrix produces binaries for all platforms
- [ ] Release workflow creates GitHub Release with assets
- [ ] Badge in README shows CI status

## Dependencies

- Depends on GDScript unit tests (phase3-vrj.3) for full value
- Can ship Go-only pipeline first, add GDScript stages incrementally

title: Multi-instance testing — automate multiple Godot instances simultaneously
description:
## Feature

Support automating multiple Godot instances simultaneously for testing networked/multiplayer games. An MCP client should be able to launch N game instances on different ports and send commands to each independently.

## Design

### Connection Management
- Current: one Connection per Server — must change
- New: named connections map: \`map[string]*godotconn.Connection\`
- Each connection has an ID (auto-generated or user-provided)

### Updated MCP Tools

**\`godot_launch\`** — add \`instance_id\` parameter
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|
| instance_id | string | no | "default" |
| port | int | no | auto-assigned |

**\`godot_connect\`** — add \`instance_id\` parameter

**All other tools** — add optional \`instance_id\` parameter (defaults to "default" for backward compat)

### New MCP Tool: \`godot_list_instances\`
Returns: \`{ instances: [{id, host, port, pid, connected, current_scene}] }\`

### New MCP Tool: \`godot_disconnect\`
| Parameter | Type | Required |
|-----------|------|----------|
| instance_id | string | yes |

Returns: \`{ disconnected, instance_id }\`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Multiple named connections coexist
- [ ] Default instance_id="default" maintains backward compat
- [ ] Auto-port assignment for launched instances
- [ ] \`godot_list_instances\` returns all active connections
- [ ] \`godot_disconnect\` cleanly closes a specific instance
- [ ] E2E tests with multiple stub servers
- [ ] Integration test: launch 2 Godot instances, send commands to each

## TDD Protocol

1. Write tests for multi-connection manager — fail
2. Refactor Server to use connection map — pass
3. Write E2E tests with 2 stubs — fail
4. Update tool handlers — pass
5. Integration test with 2 headless Godot instances

title: allow_multiple ignored in call_method addon
description:
## Summary
The `godot_call_method` MCP tool accepts an `allow_multiple` boolean
parameter and sends it to the Godot addon, but the GDScript
`method_handler.gd` ignores it entirely. It always operates on
`nodes[0]` only, so setting `allow_multiple: true` silently does
nothing.

## Repro steps
1. Connect to a running game with multiple Button nodes
2. Call `godot_call_method` with:
   - selector: "class:Button"
   - method: "get_text"
   - allow_multiple: true
3. Expected: method is called on all matched Button nodes, results
   returned for each
4. Actual: method is called only on the first matched node; the
   `allow_multiple` param is silently dropped by the addon

## Files
- Go side declares the param: `/home/mrf/Projects/godot-stagehand/internal/mcpserver/tools_method.go` line 76
- Go side sends it: tools_method.go lines 106-108
- GDScript handler ignores it: `/home/mrf/Projects/godot-stagehand/addons/stagehand/core/method_handler.gd` line 28-53

Build: 226c946

title: godot_type_text always fails: handler not registered
description: The Go MCP server's handleTypeText (tools_input.go:175) sends method "input_text" via callGodot, but the Godot addon (stagehand_server.gd _register_builtin_handlers) never registers an "input_text" handler. The function StagehandInputSimulator.input_text() exists in input_simulator.gd:169 but is never wired up to the command router. Any call to godot_type_text will return 'Method not found: input_text'. Build SHA: 68d04b2.

title: GDScript _params crashes on non-Dictionary params
description:
## Summary
The `_params()` helper in stagehand_server.gd (line 504) performs an
unchecked assignment `var d: Dictionary = params` when `params` is not
null. If a WebSocket client sends JSON-RPC params as an Array (which
is valid per JSON-RPC 2.0 spec), this line causes a runtime type error
crash in the Godot addon.

## Repro steps
1. Connect to the Stagehand WebSocket server directly (not via the
   Go MCP server)
2. Send a JSON-RPC request with params as an array:
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping","params":[]}
3. Expected: graceful error response
4. Actual: GDScript runtime error at stagehand_server.gd:504
   -- crash or unhandled error in _process loop

## Scope
All 22 registered handlers pass through `_params()`, so every method
is affected. The Go MCP server always sends Dictionary params, so
this only affects direct WebSocket clients. However, the addon is
documented as a WebSocket server accepting external connections, so
robustness against malformed input matters.

## File
`/home/mrf/Projects/godot-stagehand/addons/stagehand/autoload/stagehand_server.gd` lines 501-505

Build: 226c946

title: Screenshot diff conflates two threshold semantics
description: In internal/mcpserver/tools_visual.go, handleScreenshotDiff passes the same 'threshold' parameter to imgdiff.Compare() as the per-pixel channel delta sensitivity (line 175) AND uses it as the maximum acceptable diff ratio (line 185). The MCP tool description says 'Maximum acceptable fraction of differing pixels [0.0-1.0]' but the same value also controls per-pixel color sensitivity inside imgdiff.Compare (internal/imgdiff/diff.go line 56). At the default 0.0 this works correctly (exact match), but for any non-zero value like 0.05 the user intends 'allow 5% of pixels to differ' while it also silently ignores per-pixel color changes up to 5% of the color range. These are two independent concerns that should use separate parameters. Introduced in commit 5084543. Build SHA: fb78bc6.

title: Screenshot capture crashes: null dereference on viewport.get_texture()
description:
## Summary

Screenshot capture (`godot_screenshot`, `godot_screenshot_save_baseline`, `godot_screenshot_diff`) is non-functional. First real usage attempt fails. Other MCP tools (get_tree, etc.) work fine — connection is healthy.

## Root Cause (from code investigation)

**Critical:** `screenshot_capture.gd:30` chains `viewport.get_texture().get_image()` without null-checking `get_texture()`. If the texture is null (headless, timing, or certain configs), this crashes the addon and kills the WebSocket connection.

```gdscript
# Current (crashes):
var img: Image = viewport.get_texture().get_image()

# Fix:
var texture := viewport.get_texture()
if texture == null:
    return {"error": "Viewport texture unavailable"}
var img: Image = texture.get_image()
```

## Additional Issues Found

1. **No validation of empty screenshot data** (tools_visual.go:96) — if GDScript returns empty data, Go creates a valid-but-empty image silently
2. **`RenderingServer.frame_post_draw` has no timeout** (screenshot_capture.gd:28) — can hang indefinitely if rendering is stuck
3. **GDScript errors returned as valid results, not RPC errors** — leads to confusing base64 decode failures on the Go side instead of clear error messages
4. **Selector-not-found silently returns full viewport** instead of error (screenshot_capture.gd:21-25)

## Affected Tools

All three screenshot MCP tools share the same capture path:
- `godot_screenshot`
- `godot_screenshot_save_baseline`
- `godot_screenshot_diff`

## Repro

Connect stagehand to a running Godot game, call `godot_screenshot`. Observe failure.

title: Fix GDScript syntax errors in text/mouse input simulator
description:
input_simulator.gd has string literals where comments should be, causing parse failures:
- `event.keycode = KEY_NONE "Placeholder - actual keys handled by unicode"` — string after assignment
- `pos = ctrl.global_position + ctrl.size / 2.0 "Center of the control"` — same pattern
- At least 3 instances across input_text and input_mouse_move functions

These are outright syntax errors — the file will not parse in Godot. Replace all trailing string literals with `# comment` syntax.

Also fix:
- Unicode handling: `char.to_unicode_buffer()[0]` breaks for non-BMP characters
- Timer delays not awaited: function returns before input simulation completes

From commit 10c9eee.

title: Fix hallucinated Godot API calls in wait tools
description:
waiter.gd calls methods that don't exist in Godot's API:
- `node.property_exists(property_name)` — not a Node method. Use `property_name in node` or check property list.
- `isinstance(actual_value is CallableBuiltIn)` — `CallableBuiltIn` is not a valid GDScript type. Use `typeof()` checks instead.

Same `property_exists()` bug is duplicated in the example project (examples/minimal-game waiter.gd lines 47, 57, 109, 149).

From commits 538d5d4 and d905550.

title: Add safety boundaries to evaluate and call_method tools
description:
Two tools allow arbitrary code execution with no restrictions:

1. **expression_evaluator.gd**: `Expression.parse()` + `expr.execute()` runs any GDScript expression the caller sends. No whitelist of safe functions, no sandbox. Can execute system calls.

2. **method_handler.gd**: `node.callv(method_name, args)` calls any method on any node. Can invoke `_ready()`, `queue_free()`, or other destructive internal methods.

Options:
- Whitelist safe methods/functions
- Add an opt-in "unsafe mode" flag that defaults to restricted
- At minimum, block methods starting with `_` (private/lifecycle)

Also fix type error: `get_node_or_null()` returns `Node`, not `Array[Node]`.

From commit 393623b.

title: Addon installation breaks host project compilation (GDScript parse errors)
description:
## Problem

Installing the Stagehand addon into a real Godot project (tested with water-wars) prevents the HOST project from compiling. The addon itself has GDScript errors that Godot's parser catches at project load time, blocking all compilation.

## Root Causes

### 1. Invalid `error_string()` calls
- `autoload/stagehand_server.gd:39` — `error_string(err)` may not exist as a global in all Godot 4.x versions
- `autoload/stagehand_server.gd:83` — same
- `core/scene_handler.gd:22` — same

### 2. Invalid `parent.tree` property access
- `core/selector_engine.gd:322` — uses `parent.tree` but Node has no `.tree` property. Must be `parent.get_tree()`.

## Impact

**Showstopper.** Any Godot project that installs this addon cannot compile. Manual testing proved this — the addon blocked water-wars from building.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All GDScript files parse without errors in Godot 4.2+ (test with `--check-only` or `--headless --quit`)
- [ ] Addon installed into a clean Godot project does NOT break compilation
- [ ] Add a CI/smoke check that validates addon GDScript parses cleanly

## TDD Protocol

Write a test (Go integration test that launches Godot with the addon and asserts clean startup) BEFORE fixing the GDScript. The test must fail first, then pass after the fix.

title: change_scene GWP handler implemented but not registered in server

## Evidence

- `scene_handler.gd` exists with `change_scene()` method but is never imported or instantiated

3. Verify the E2E test passes

title: Integration test GetTree assertion fails — checks wrong node path

godot_integration_test.go:117: get_tree result missing Label; raw={"children":[...{"class":"Label","name":"titleLabel","path":"/root/TestScene/UICanvas/titleLabel"...}

title: wait_for_node: implement state parameter (exists/visible/removed)
description:
## Problem

DESIGN.md specifies `godot_wait_for_node` should accept a `state` parameter with values `"exists"`, `"visible"`, `"removed"` (default: `"exists"`). Current implementation only checks existence — no visibility or removal detection.

## Current State

- Go tool (tools_wait.go): no `state` parameter in tool definition
- GDScript (waiter.gd:68-78): only checks `results.size() > 0` — existence only

## Spec (from DESIGN.md)

| state | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| `"exists"` | Wait until selector matches at least one node (current behavior) |
| `"visible"` | Wait until matched node has `visible == true` |
| `"removed"` | Wait until selector matches zero nodes (inverse of exists) |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Go tool definition includes `state` string parameter with enum constraint
- [ ] GDScript waiter handles all three state values
- [ ] Unit test for each state in Go (E2E with stub)
- [ ] Integration test with real Godot for at least `exists` and `visible`

## TDD Protocol

1. Add state parameter to Go tool definition and write E2E tests for all 3 states — tests fail
2. Update stub to handle state-aware responses
3. Update waiter.gd to implement state checks
4. Tests pass

title: Validate selectors in Go handlers before sending to Godot
description:
## Problem

The Go selector parser (`internal/selector/parse.go`) exists and correctly validates selector syntax, but NO tool handler actually calls it. All handlers pass raw selector strings directly to Godot without validation. Invalid selectors fail silently in GDScript instead of returning clear errors from the Go layer.

## Evidence

- `selector.Parse()` and `selector.ParseChain()` exist with full test coverage
- Grep for `selector.Parse` in `internal/mcpserver/` returns zero results
- Example: `tools_wait.go:35` passes `selector` directly to params map

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All Go tool handlers that accept a `selector` parameter validate it through `selector.ParseChain()` before sending to Godot
- [ ] Invalid selectors return a clear MCP error with the parse failure message
- [ ] Unit tests verify that invalid selectors are rejected at the Go layer
- [ ] Valid selectors still pass through unchanged

## TDD Protocol

1. Write tests in `server_test.go` that call handlers with invalid selectors and expect MCP errors
2. Tests fail (currently invalid selectors pass through)
3. Add validation to each handler
4. Tests pass

title: Wait tools hang forever if game process exits or WebSocket disconnects
description:
## Summary

`godot_wait_for_signal`, `godot_wait_for_node`, and `godot_wait_for_property` all block indefinitely if the Godot game process dies, the player loses (causing scene change/exit), or the game window is closed while a wait is in progress.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `godot_wait_for_signal` (or similar wait tool) on a signal that hasn't fired yet
2. Close the game window / kill the Godot process / trigger game-over
3. Observe the MCP tool call never returns

## Expected Behavior

Wait tools should detect WebSocket disconnection and return an error (e.g., `"error": "connection lost while waiting for signal X"`) within a reasonable timeout.

## Actual Behavior

The MCP server hangs forever waiting for a response that will never arrive.

## Impact

Any automation or test script using wait tools becomes permanently stuck if the game exits unexpectedly. Requires manual kill of the MCP process.

## Suggested Fix

- Detect WebSocket close/error in the wait loop and abort with a descriptive error
- Optionally add a configurable timeout parameter to all wait tools (default e.g. 30s)

title: Screenshot tools skip selector validation
description: handleScreenshot, handleSaveBaseline, and handleScreenshotDiff in tools_visual.go all accept an optional 'selector' parameter but none call validateSelector() before sending the selector to Godot. Every other handler that accepts a selector (find_nodes, get_property, set_property, click, type_text, mouse_move, wait_for_node, wait_for_signal, wait_for_property, call_method, evaluate) validates first. An invalid selector like 'name:' sent to the screenshot tools would bypass Go-side validation and be sent raw to Godot, inconsistent with the stated convention in CLAUDE.md: 'Validate selectors in Go with selector.ParseChain() before sending to Godot'. Introduced in phase3-vrj.5 (commit 5084543) and not caught in the recent screenshot diff threshold refactor (7aae266). Build SHA: 877e8ed. File: internal/mcpserver/tools_visual.go lines 74, 98-101.

title: godot_evaluate context_node param silently ignored
description: The Go MCP server (tools_method.go:138) sends the context_node parameter as key "context_node" in the JSON-RPC params dict, but the Godot expression_evaluator.gd (line 24) reads the key "selector" instead. This means the context_node parameter on godot_evaluate is silently ignored -- expressions always evaluate against tree.root regardless of what context_node is specified. Repro: call godot_evaluate(expression="self.name", context_node="/root/Main/Player") -- will return the root node's name instead of the Player node's name. Build SHA: 68d04b2.

Set up the Go module (go.mod), directory structure per DESIGN.md, and a CLAUDE.md with project conventions.

Directories:
- internal/mcpserver/
- internal/godotconn/
- internal/selector/
- addons/playwright/autoload/
- addons/playwright/core/
- addons/playwright/protocol/
- testdata/test_project/

Also: main.go stub, .gitignore, CLAUDE.md with build/test/lint commands.
